rv.q: "The Counter" achieves that only intermittently. The rest of the time it's over too easy: well-done at the edges, runny in the middle.

Add Anthony Edwards and Susannah Flood, two excellent actors who illuminate the not-at-all generic inner lives of the seemingly simple characters, and the silent-but-canny directorial hand of David Cromer, and you've got an intensely provocative new American play.
He deftly handles the new play's pathos and its bleak wit, and culls nuanced, moving performances from the actors.
But these are simply better plays. Too much of what the characters say and do in 'The Counter' feels imposed by the playwright.

cn.t: Kennedy's diner drama about two lonely souls forging an unlikely friendship features strong performances from Edwards and Flood, but critics find the play itself uneven—some praise its intriguing character work while others call it shaggy and predictable.
